record.paper_title: Brane Supersymmetry Breaking and the Cosmological Constant: Open Problems
record.original_question: Do the higher Kaluza-Klein excitations in these compactifications make substantial contributions to the four-dimensional cosmological constant through Str M^2_bulk or Str M^4_bulk, or is there a real mechanism that suppresses or cancels their effect? The scenario requires either that the Kaluza-Klein tower also obey Str M^2_bulk = 0 and contributes negligibly to Str M^4_bulk, for example because the mass splittings are tiny, or that some other unexpected feature of the effective four-dimensional Kaluza-Klein gauge theory removes these contributions.

evidence.quote: It must be assumed that Kaluza Klein modes do not contribute to the 4–dimensional cosmological constant, e.g. because their mass splittings might be very small.

What is a potentially fatal problem with our scenario, though, is the following. So far, we have only considered the contribution of the Kaluza–Klein zero modes to both Str M4 bulk and Str M2 bulk. But the higher Kaluza–Klein modes should also contribute.

We must assume that Str M2 bulk = 0 also for the Kaluza–Klein modes, and moreover, that they do not contribute to Str M4 bulk – either because their mass splittings are tiny, or because of some other unexpected feature of the effective four–dimensional Kaluza–Klein gauge theory.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a brane-world scenario in which our four-dimensional universe is realized as a 3-brane embedded in a higher-dimensional spacetime with compact transverse dimensions. Assume that supersymmetry is broken on the brane at a scale of order the TeV, while in the bulk supergravity sector supersymmetry is broken at a much smaller scale (of order the meV). Let M denote the mass operator of the bulk fields and let

  Str M^{2k} = ∑_J (-1)^{2J} (2J+1) m_J^{2k}

denote the supertrace over bulk states, where the sum is taken over all bulk particle species J with mass m_J. The zero-mode sector of the Kaluza–Klein reduction is assumed to satisfy Str M^2_bulk = 0 and to contribute negligibly to Str M^4_bulk, which is required for the four-dimensional cosmological constant to come out of the observed (small) order of magnitude.

The higher Kaluza–Klein modes (the nonzero modes of the compactification) also contribute to the one-loop vacuum energy. The problem is:

Determine whether the higher Kaluza–Klein excitations of the bulk fields can make substantial contributions to the four-dimensional cosmological constant through Str M^2_bulk or Str M^4_bulk, or whether there exists a genuine mechanism in the effective four-dimensional Kaluza–Klein gauge theory that ensures both
 (i) Str M^2_bulk = 0 for the full Kaluza–Klein tower, and
 (ii) the contribution of the tower to Str M^4_bulk is negligible (for instance because the supersymmetry-breaking mass splittings inside each Kaluza–Klein level are sufficiently small, or because of some other structural feature of the four-dimensional effective theory).

Either exhibit such a suppression/cancellation mechanism, or show that no such mechanism exists.

artifact.status_search_result: The question of whether Kaluza–Klein towers in brane supersymmetry breaking scenarios contribute to the four-dimensional cosmological constant via Str M^2 or Str M^4 was raised as an open assumption, and subsequent literature on technically natural cosmological constants from 6D brane backreaction and on string compactifications continues to treat it as an unresolved problem with no widely accepted cancellation mechanism for the full KK tower. No definitive solution was located.

status_evidence.title: Brane supersymmetry breaking and the cosmological constant: open problems
status_evidence.snippet: Str M^2 = 0 must also hold for the Kaluza-Klein modes... either because their mass splittings are tiny, or because of some other unexpected feature.
status_evidence.claim: The original formulation explicitly leaves the Kaluza-Klein contribution as an open assumption.

status_evidence.title: Technically natural cosmological constant from supersymmetric 6D brane backreaction
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses bulk SUSY breaking and KK contributions to vacuum energy in brane scenarios.
status_evidence.claim: Later work continues to investigate but does not definitively resolve KK contributions to the 4D cosmological constant.
